hints: Collect the $\sin\theta$ terms on one side and the $\cos\theta$ terms on the other.
Divide by $\cos\theta$ to form an exact equation for $\tan\theta$.
Use the sign of the tangent and the interval $0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$ to decide how many angular solutions are valid.
walkthrough:
Substitute the exact trigonometric values $\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$:
$$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin\theta - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos\theta + \cos\theta = 2\sin\theta$$
$$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin\theta + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos\theta = 2\sin\theta$$

Multiply the entire equation by 2 to clear fractions:
$$\sqrt{3}\sin\theta + \cos\theta = 4\sin\theta$$

Isolate $\cos\theta$ on the left and collect terms in $\sin\theta$ on the right:
$$\cos\theta = 4\sin\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta = (4 - \sqrt{3})\sin\theta$$

Divide by $(4 - \sqrt{3})\cos\theta$ to express in terms of $\tan\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{4 - \sqrt{3}}$$
